subject: Re: Redwood model fit + quantization follow-ups (FinWave)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liz Chen <liz@finwave.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@finwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-15T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: FinWave discovery notes + next steps (model fit / quantization)

Hi Liz / Samir 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and the next steps we discussed: 

Recap
- Primary goal: ship a low-latency assistant for customer docs & billing workflows (avg response < 400ms p50 for 512-token responses, target throughput 20k tokens/sec regionally).
- Hard constraint: PII must not be stored in hosted logs; you prefer Private deployment or Dedicated with KMS.
- Evaluation: you have an internal eval set (~2k prompts) and a small human-review panel for quality checks.

Recommended short list to validate on your eval set
1) Redwood-RW-13B-instruct (baseline  best cost / latency tradeoff)
2) Llama-2-70B-chat (higher quality on long-context summarization)
3) Mistral-7B-Instruct (compact option with good instruction-following)

Quantization/throughput trade studies to run
- AWQ 4-bit: best throughput with modest quality delta on many instruction sets
- GPTQ 4-bit: often slightly better quality, slower compile/runtime on some kernels
- FP8 (experimental): good throughput on newer hw; regression risk higher on specialized prompts

Next steps (agreed)
- We’ll run your eval prompts against the three model candidates in floating-point and AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit where supported. (Action: Redwood - marissa + rishi)
- Please share a sample of 200 representative prompts (we called this the "pilot set").
- We’ll return a short trade study (quant vs perf vs quality) and a recommended canary plan.

Attachments: finwave_eval_promptset_v1.csv (sample prompt set), quant_tradeoff_notes.pdf (previous trade study summary).

I’ll loop Rishi as our SE to scope the A/B runs and expected runtime/cost. Any corrections to the recap, flag them and I’ll update.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Liz Chen <liz@finwave.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@finwave.ai>, procurements@finwave.ai
Date: 2027-09-15T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinWave discovery notes + next steps (model fit / quantization)

Thanks Marissa  this is great and mostly matches our notes. A couple quick clarifications/questions before we hand you the pilot set: 

1) For throughput targets: the 20k tokens/sec is across our multi-region deployment (US + EU). Per-region steady throughput target is ~812k tokens/sec. Can you scope the trade study per-region?
2) On quantization: our priority is avoiding any customer-visible regression on billing Q&A and refund-policy summarization (high-precision legal language). How often do you see regressions when moving from FP16 -> AWQ 4-bit vs FP16 -> GPTQ 4-bit?
3) Security: we need to confirm that Redwood Dedicated will keep telemetry out of hosted logs; procurement will ask for SOC2 evidence.

Looping in procurements for the SOW timeline. We can share the 200 pilot prompts by EOD Monday once we validate PII redaction.


Liz Chen
Head of ML Engineering, FinWave
liz@finwave.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liz Chen <liz@finwave.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@finwave.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-16T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FinWave discovery notes + next steps (model fit / quantization)

Hi Liz  great questions, answers below and a proposed plan.

Throughput scope
- We’ll report per-region throughput numbers (us / eu) and an aggregated projection for the multi-region config. We’ll include latency p50/p95 for 128/512-token responses.

Observed regressions (FP16 -> quantized)  summary from prior FinWave-like workloads:
- AWQ 4-bit: typical quality delta small for instruction-following (~113% on our internal ranking metrics, negligible on short Q&A), occasional edge regressions on exact-match legal phrasing.
- GPTQ 4-bit: slightly better fidelity on nuanced language (~0.51% better than AWQ on our evals) but runtime can be 101325% slower depending on kernel availability.
- FP8: promising on H100-class hw for throughput; more variability on smaller models and some hallucination risk on longer context QA.

Concrete plan (what Redwood will deliver)
1) Run your pilot set (200 prompts) across the 3 model candidates in: FP16, AWQ-4bit, GPTQ-4bit (where supported).
2) Produce a one-pager summarizing: per-model quality metrics (accuracy / accept-rate / top-1 human pass), latency/throughput numbers (tokens/sec), cost estimate delta.
3) Provide model prompt-set examples that triggered regressions and recommended prompt adjustments or fallback policies.

Preliminary ballpark numbers (subject to exact infra)
- RW-13B (AWQ-4bit) on H100: ~1822k tok/s per GPU (512-token median latency ~150220ms).
- Llama-70B (GPTQ-4bit) on H100: ~812k tok/s per GPU (512-token median latency ~220350ms).

Attachments included: finwave_evals_v1.csv (sample run outputs), quant_tradeoff_notes.pdf (trade-study with prior customers). Also linking our public benchmark page: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/FW-2387

If that plan looks good I’ll schedule the runs  we’ll need the pilot set and confirmation on whether you want private (VPC) runs or dedicated-hosted runs.


Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

On Thu, Sep 16, 2027 at 9:30 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Liz  great questions, answers below and a proposed plan.

Thanks  looping in a couple of operational details from the SE side. Proposed A/B test/run plan: 
- We’ll run the pilot on Redwood Dedicated in your region (us-east) to match network characteristics. If you prefer Private, we can run the same jobs inside your VPC; we’ll need an SG/WAF checklist to confirm egress rules.
- Acceptance criteria: we’ll produce per-prompt deltas and flag regressions where model output difference causes a human reviewer to mark "fail" for the use-case. If regressions > 3% on billing Q&A, we’ll recommend a fallback to FP16 for that route.
- Timeline: 3 business days to run the pilot once we have the prompt set + 1 live reviewer.

Action items for FinWave
- Share the 200 pilot prompts (redacted for PII) + 1 human reviewer contact.
- Confirm preferred infra (Dedicated-us vs VPC-private).

I’ll open a HubSpot ticket for tracking and post the run results to the Drive link.


Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Liz
